title: Integrate NellDB as persistent memory and configuration backend
description:
Replace SQLite+FTS5+file-based storage with NellDB, Sam's existing distributed document database. NellDB provides:

- **nell.Store interface**: Put, Get, Delete, List, ListAll, Query, GetChangesSince, SearchSimilar (vector search)
- **sdk.DocDB**: Document database with MVCC revisions
- **logstore**: Durable Zstd-compressed append-only log
- **sdk.Replicator**: Multi-primary HTTP replication with HLC knowledge vectors
- **Vector search**: HNSW + PCA + PQ for semantic memory
- **HTTP server**: Standalone binary on port 9342

Plan:

1. Add NellDB as a dependency (go get github.com/samcharles93/NellDB)
2. Create internal/nell/ adapter package wrapping nell.Store for archie-core's data models
3. Collections: sessions, messages, memory, config, tasks
4. Replace internal/store (SQLite) with NellDB backend
5. Replace file-based MEMORY.md with nell collections + vector search
6. Wire into cmd/archied/main.go as the storage backend

This gives archie-core multi-primary replication for free — two archied instances on different hosts can sync state without a central database.

Ref: /work/apps/nell-engine/ (store.go, types.go, sdk/docdb.go, server/)
acceptance_criteria: archied starts with a NellDB backend instead of SQLite. Sessions and messages persist across restarts. Vector search returns semantically similar messages. Two archied instances can replicate state via nell sync.

title: [EPIC] Tools: central registry, MCP client, guardrails
description:
Central tool infrastructure to match Hermes parity:

1. **Tool registry**: A central registry where tool modules register themselves with name, schema, handler, toolset membership, and availability check. Dynamic discovery of built-in tools. This replaces the current pattern of manually constructing core.ToolSet maps per invocation.

2. **MCP client**: Connect to external MCP servers via stdio, HTTP/StreamableHTTP, or SSE transport. Discover their tools and register them into the tool registry. Support automatic reconnection with backoff, configurable timeouts, per-server parallel tool call opt-in.

3. **Guardrails**: Tool-call loop detection (repeated calls, repeated failures, no-progress loops). Idempotent/mutating tool classification. Warning vs hard-stop decisions.

4. **Progressive disclosure**: When tool schemas exceed a context-window threshold, replace them with bridge tools (tool_search/tool_describe/tool_call) and surface on demand. Core tools are always visible.

Ref: docs/prds/hermes-gap-analysis.md section 3
acceptance_criteria: MCP servers can be configured with a TOML block and their tools appear alongside built-ins. The agent loop is protected against tool-call loops. Tool schemas stay within context budget.

title: [EPIC] Memory: pluggable provider architecture with file-backed persistence
description:
Pluggable memory system to match Hermes parity:

1. **MemoryProvider interface**: Abstract interface with methods for initialize(), get_tool_schemas(), prefetch(), sync_turn(), and optional lifecycle hooks (on_session_end, on_session_switch, on_pre_compress, on_memory_write).

2. **Built-in file-backed memory**: MEMORY.md and USER.md stored per-session/profile. LLM-callable memory tool with add/replace/remove actions. Frozen snapshot at session start (preserves prefix cache), immediate disk write on updates. Section-sign delimited entries with substring matching.

3. **MemoryManager**: Orchestrates built-in + at most one external provider. Background serialized write executor. Prefetch with timeout (8s). Streaming context scrubber that strips injected memory spans from model output.

Ref: docs/prds/hermes-gap-analysis.md section 4
acceptance_criteria: An external memory provider (e.g. Honcho, Mem0) can be plugged in via config. The built-in memory tool persists across sessions. Conversation context is recalled on session resume.

title: [EPIC] Gateway: rich message model, adapter lifecycle, session management
description:
Foundational gateway infrastructure to match Hermes parity. Three interdependent pieces:

1. **Message model**: Replace the 3-field Message struct with a rich MessageEvent (MessageType enum: text/photo/video/audio/voice/document/sticker/command, media_urls, reply_to context, metadata dict, source). This is the wire type every adapter produces.

2. **Adapter lifecycle**: Replace the 3-method Gateway interface with a BasePlatformAdapter interface: connect()/disconnect()/send() as required methods, plus optional overrides for typing indicators, edit/delete, image/voice/video/document send, interactive UX (clarify buttons, approval dialogs). Capability flags (supports_code_blocks, splits_long_messages, supports_async_delivery).

3. **Session management**: SessionSource struct (platform, chat_id, chat_type, user_id, thread_id, guild_id, profile), AsyncSessionStore for persistent session storage, SessionContext for system prompt injection.

All three blocks together enable adding new platforms as plugins without touching core gateway code.

Ref: docs/prds/hermes-gap-analysis.md sections 1-2
acceptance_criteria: New adapters can be added by implementing a Go interface with connect/disconnect/send + optional media methods. Messages carry full metadata through the pipeline. Sessions persist across gateway restarts.

title: Spawned archie-agent containers not on daemon's docker network — can't reach NATS
description: Root cause of 'agent still failing on the server': archied's container.Pool.Acquire creates archie-agent containers via the Docker SDK with no NetworkMode set, so Docker attaches them to the default bridge network. archied and nats run on the compose-created 'archie-core_default' network instead, so the spawned container's hostname resolution for 'nats' (from NATS_URL=nats://nats:4222) fails and archie-agent can't connect. Confirmed on carina host logs: archied logs show repeating 'taskrun request failed err="nats: no responders available for request"' for every task, containers created and destroyed within ~1.5s (consistent with archie-agent's NATS client failing fast). Fixed by detecting the daemon's own container's network in NewPool (selfNetwork, via ContainerInspect on os.Hostname()) and setting HostConfig.NetworkMode on spawned containers to match.
close_reason: Fix already implemented and verified: selfNetwork() in internal/container/pool.go detects the daemon's own container network via ContainerInspect(os.Hostname()) and Acquire() sets HostConfig.NetworkMode to match, so spawned archie-agent containers join the same compose network as nats. Build and internal/container tests pass.

title: Session persistence: SQLite+FTS5 conversation store
description:
Persistent conversation history with full-text search. Required for multi-session chat memory (archie-core-abg.6) and gateway session management.

1. **SessionStore**: SQLite tables for sessions (session_id, source, created_at, updated_at) and messages (session_id, role, content, timestamp, metadata).
2. **FTS5**: Full-text search over message content for memory recall.
3. **Session splitting**: When compression occurs, child sessions link to parent via parent_session_id.
4. **WAL mode**: Concurrent readers + one writer.

This replaces the current ephemeral approach where messages are lost after the agent exits.

Ref: docs/prds/hermes-gap-analysis.md section 4, gateway/session.py
acceptance_criteria: Conversation history persists across daemon restarts. FTS5 search returns relevant messages. Compression creates child sessions without data loss.

title: Feature-based config: split monolithic config.toml into modular files
description:
Sam's explicit directive: move to feature-based config files instead of one monolithic config.toml. This is infrastructure that makes everything else easier to build and test.

Proposed structure:
- ~/.config/archie/config.toml (daemon-level: work_dir, db_path, poll_interval, max_retries)
- ~/.config/archie/identities.d/*.toml (one file per identity)
- ~/.config/archie/gateway.toml (chat channels, platform configs)
- ~/.config/archie/tools.toml (MCP servers, tool policy)
- ~/.config/archie/memory.toml (memory provider config)
- ~/.config/archie/models.toml (LLM providers and model config)

Design constraints:
- Each file is self-contained and validated independently
- Missing files mean "feature disabled" — no error
- Overlay support preserved (--config-overlay still works, applies to all files in the directory)
- Backward compat: if feature files don't exist, read from legacy monolithic config.toml
- No hardcoded file paths — configurable via [config] paths block

This enables building features independently without merge conflicts in a single monster struct.
acceptance_criteria: A new feature (e.g. MCP) can be configured by adding one new TOML file. No changes to existing config parsing code are needed. Legacy monolithic config.toml still works.

title: CLI: command registry framework with plugin-contributed commands
description:
Interactive CLI framework to match Hermes parity. Not a dashboard — just a command-line interface for operational control.

1. **CommandDef registry**: Name, description, category, handler, aliases. Commands register themselves at init time.
2. **Subcommands**: Plugin-contributed commands via a RegisterCommand hook.
3. **Essential commands**: 
   - archied run (current default, unchanged)
   - archied status (daemon + task summary)
   - archied config get/set (read/write config entries)
   - archied gateway start/stop/restart/status
   - archied model list/switch
   - archied profile create/list/use
   - archied doctor (diagnostics)
   - archied version

This is a Go-native CLI (no external framework needed — just flag.FlagSet and consistent patterns). The gateway already works; this adds the CLI surface for managing it.

Ref: docs/prds/hermes-gap-analysis.md section 6
acceptance_criteria: archied status shows daemon health + task counts. archied config get bot_user works. archied gateway status shows connected platforms. Plugin-registered commands appear in help output.

title: Wire Layer 2 core plugin loader into archied startup
description: internal/plugin/plugin.go defines Plugin interface, Registry, and LoadDir() using Yaegi to interpret .go files from a directory, but nothing in cmd/archied/main.go calls it. Wire ~/.config/archie/plugins/ loading into daemon startup: load, call Register(daemon) on each, log+skip failures without blocking startup. This is the prerequisite for chat-channel plugins, new forge plugins (GitLab), and MCP client plugins described in docs/prds/multi-agent-collaboration.md phase A.
design: Reuse internal/plugin/plugin.go as-is per the v2 PRD reconciliation note (sec.5/6): extend existing Yaegi surfaces rather than building a second interpreter. Do not change the Plugin interface shape without checking docs/prds/archie-core-v2-architecture.md sec.5 first.
acceptance_criteria: archied loads .go plugin files from ~/.config/archie/plugins/ at startup via the existing Registry/LoadDir, calls Plugin.Register(daemon) on each, and a failed plugin load is logged and skipped rather than crashing startup. Existing daemon startup tests remain green.
close_reason: Already implemented: cmd/archied/main.go loads cfg.PluginDir via plugin.LoadDir(dir, pluginextract.Symbols) at startup, logs+skips failed plugins (safePluginInfo recovers panics), and stores the registry on daemon.Daemon.PluginRegistry. Build and internal/plugin + cmd/archied tests pass. Note for downstream work (abg.5 chat channels, abg.9 MCP, abg.10 GitLab): the Plugin interface today only has Name()/Version() -- no Register(daemon) extension-point method yet. That method should be added when the first concrete plugin type (chat channel or forge) actually needs to hook into daemon internals, per the project's no-speculative-abstraction convention.

title: Test forge fakes missing LinkBranch method broke go vet/test for whole module
description: forge.Forge gained LinkBranch(ctx, owner, repo, issueNumber, branch) error in the branch-linking feature (ff4c51e) but the hand-rolled test doubles (stubForge in cmd/archied/main_test.go, prCapturingForge in cmd/archie-agent/taskrun_test.go, testForge in internal/daemon/daemon_test.go, fakeForge in internal/forgerpc/forgerpc_test.go) never got the method added, so they stopped satisfying forge.Forge. This broke go vet ./... and go test ./... for the entire module, not just those 4 packages, since go vet type-checks all test files as part of module vet. Fixed by adding LinkBranch stubs to all four fakes.
close_reason: Added LinkBranch stub methods to stubForge, prCapturingForge, testForge, and fakeForge. go build/vet/test ./... now clean across the whole module.

title: config.docker.toml missing required fields, no overlay merge implemented
description: config.docker.toml was rewritten to be a docs-as-overlay file (comment says base+overlay merge) but internal/config.Load has no merge logic and docker-compose.yml mounts only config.docker.toml at /etc/archie/config.toml. It is missing bot_user, [forge], [dispatch], [models], [providers], [budgets] which Load requires -> daemon fails to start in docker as currently configured. Implement real base+overlay config loading (or restore a full standalone docker config) so there is one source of truth.
close_reason: Implemented config.LoadOverlay (base decode + overlay decode into same struct, then shared finalize/validate), wired -config-overlay flag in cmd/archied, fixed docker-compose.yml to mount both base config.toml and config.docker.toml overlay, minimized config.docker.toml to true diff-only overlay, added tests proving overlay-omitted required fields (bot_user, repos) still come from base.

title: Daemon: process multiple tasks concurrently (max_concurrency enforcement)
description: Daemon currently processes one task at a time (docs/prds/archie-core-v2-architecture.md Phase 2). This is the core blocker between current state and any multi-agent scaling mode — needed before container max_concurrency or same-repo concurrency can matter. Wire the daemon's dispatch loop to run N tasks in parallel, respecting a configurable max_concurrency.
design: internal/container/pool.go already enforces max_concurrency for container lifecycle — reuse that limit/pattern in the daemon's task dispatch rather than inventing a second concurrency control.
acceptance_criteria: Daemon dispatch loop runs multiple tasks concurrently up to a configured max_concurrency limit; single-task-at-a-time behavior is gone.
close_reason: Implemented concurrent SQLite and NATS task dispatch using containers.max_concurrency, with default same-repo serialization and race-tested dispatcher coverage.

title: Webhook platform: generic inbound adapter with HMAC + filters + templates
description:
Generic webhook platform adapter:

1. **HTTP server**: Receives POSTs from external services (GitHub, GitLab, Stripe, etc.). Per-route configuration.
2. **HMAC validation**: GitHub (X-Hub-Signature-256), GitLab (X-Gitlab-Token), Svix/AgentMail, generic V2 (timestamp-bound replay protection), legacy V1.
3. **Declarative filters**: all/any/not, field resolution (dot-notation), equals/contains/regex, in_file.
4. **Script transforms**: External bash/python scripts per route that transform or filter payloads.
5. **Prompt templates**: Dot-notation template rendering from webhook payloads ({pull_request.title}).
6. **deliver_only mode**: Skip agent, render prompt as deliverable message (push notifications at zero LLM cost).
7. **Idempotency cache**: TTL-based dedup of webhook retries.

Ref: docs/prds/hermes-gap-analysis.md (webhook.py, webhook_filters.py, msgraph_webhook.py)
acceptance_criteria: A GitHub webhook lands on /webhooks/github, passes HMAC validation, renders a prompt from the PR payload, and the agent responds. Duplicate deliveries are deduped.

title: Context compression: aux model summarization pipeline
description:
Conversation compression pipeline:

1. **Auxiliary model client**: Dedicated cheap/fast model for summarization. Probes context window feasibility at startup.
2. **Compression templates**: Structured summaries with Resolved/Pending question tracking. Head and tail context protection.
3. **Iterative summary merging**: Multiple compression rounds, tool output pruning before LLM summarization.
4. **Session splitting**: Rotate session_id on compression, link child → parent.
5. **Image size recovery**: Re-encode oversized base64 images at smaller size.
6. **Pluggable context engine**: ABC with should_compress/compress/on_session_end lifecycle for third-party replacements.

Ref: docs/prds/hermes-gap-analysis.md section 1.2 (conversation_compression.py, context_compressor.py, context_engine.py)
acceptance_criteria: When a conversation approaches context limit, the auxiliary model summarizes middle turns. Session rotates to a child session. The agent continues without losing context.

title: Operations: readiness probes + drain control + systemd notify
description:
Production operations infrastructure:

1. **Readiness probes**: Multi-check system — state_db (read-only probe), config (parse check), disk (<90%), model (configured), gateway (running/draining + connected count). Return overall ok or degraded.
2. **Drain control**: Marker file (~/.archie/.drain_request.json) for external drain triggers. Instantiation epoch (boot_id + PID 1 start time) to distinguish restart types.
3. **Shutdown watchdog**: Out-of-loop os.Exit backstop if shutdown exceeds leash (drain timeout + 60s grace).
4. **systemd notify**: sd_notify integration — watchdog with loop-progress sampling, ready status on startup.

Ref: docs/prds/hermes-gap-analysis.md section 9-10 (readiness.py, drain_control.py, shutdown_watchdog.py, systemd_notify.py)
acceptance_criteria: GET /health returns JSON with per-subsystem status. systemd watchdog fires if the event loop stalls. Drain requests initiate graceful shutdown.

title: API server: OpenAI-compatible REST endpoint for sessions and runs
description:
OpenAI-compatible REST API for external tool integration:

1. **Chat Completions**: POST /v1/chat/completions — stateless, with X-Hermes-Session-Id for continuity.
2. **Responses API**: POST /v1/responses — stateful via previous_response_id.
3. **Sessions**: CRUD + fork for session management.
4. **Runs**: POST /v1/runs (returns run_id immediately), GET /v1/runs/{id} (status), GET /v1/runs/{id}/events (SSE stream), POST /v1/runs/{id}/approval and /stop (resolve or interrupt).
5. **Models**: GET /v1/models — list configured models.
6. **Health**: GET /health (simple), GET /health/detailed (authenticated readiness).

This enables Open WebUI, LobeChat, and other OpenAI-compatible frontends to use archie-core as a backend.

Ref: docs/prds/hermes-gap-analysis.md (api_server.py)
acceptance_criteria: curl -X POST /v1/chat/completions with a model and messages returns a streaming response. Sessions persist across requests via session ID. Runs can be stopped mid-execution.

title: Delivery system: router, ledger, dead targets, wake
description:
Outbound message delivery infrastructure built on NATS JetStream (already provides guaranteed delivery, dead-letter queues, ack/nak, dedup — no need for a separate actor engine like Hollywood).

1. **DeliveryTarget**: Parse strings like 'telegram:12345' or 'discord:channel:thread'. Resolve to platform adapter.
2. **DeliveryRouter**: Route content to configured targets, handle truncation, silence-narration filtering.
3. **DeliveryLedger**: JetStream consumer with max-deliver=3, ack-wait configurable per target. Crash recovery via NATS redelivery (no separate SQLite ledger needed).
4. **DeadTargetRegistry**: Persistent JSON tracking of confirmed-dead targets (deleted groups, kicked bots). Self-healing on successful send.
5. **Wake delivery**: Use NATS request/reply for async delivery to push-capable adapters.
acceptance_criteria: A cron job can schedule a message for delivery. If the target is unreachable, the ledger retries. If the bot is kicked from a group, the target is registered dead and skipped.

title: Cron/scheduling: job store, ticker, blueprints
description:
Scheduled automation system:

1. **Job store**: JSON file per profile (~/.archie/cron/jobs.json) with cross-process file locking. CRUD operations.
2. **Ticker engine**: Configurable interval, parallel/sequential thread pools, delivery resolution via DeliveryRouter.
3. **Blueprints**: Parameterized automation templates with typed slots (time, enum, text, weekdays). Form schema for CLI/gateway consumption.
4. **Lifecycle guard**: Rejects cron job specs containing dangerous commands (gateway restart, systemctl, launchctl, pkill).

Ref: docs/prds/hermes-gap-analysis.md section 1 (cron/)
acceptance_criteria: A cron job can be created to send a daily status summary. Jobs persist across restarts. Dangerous commands are rejected at creation time.

title: Security: pairing device auth + per-platform authorization
description:
Authorization infrastructure to match Hermes parity:

1. **PairingStore**: Cryptographic code generation (8-char from 32-char unambiguous alphabet, no 0/O/1/I), salted SHA-256 hashing, constant-time comparison, 1-hour expiry, rate limiting (1/10min per user), lockout after 5 failures. File-backed with atomic writes (chmod 0600).

2. **Auth mixin**: Layered authorization for gateway messages: per-platform allowlists → role auth → relay delegation → pairing store → deny. Per-platform env var patterns (TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS, DISCORD_ALLOWED_USERS, etc.).

3. **Slash command access**: Admin/non-admin command gating. Admin users (allow_admin_from) get all commands. Non-admin get user_allowed_commands. help and whoami always allowed.

Ref: docs/prds/hermes-gap-analysis.md section 5
acceptance_criteria: Unknown users receive a pairing code instead of agent access. Admin users can run all slash commands. Unauthorized users get a configurable response (pair or ignore).

title: Chat channel write actions: spawn/approve/cancel through daemon review gate
description: Follow-up to archie-core-abg.5 (channel interface + read-only Telegram). Define the semantics for chat-triggered dispatch (there is no Gitea issue behind a chat-initiated task -- needs its own store/task creation path) and wire /spawn, /approve, /cancel slash commands through the same daemon review/gatekeeping that issue-driven dispatch uses. Blocked on abg.5 (interface must exist first) and should be sequenced after multi-identity daemon core (abg.4) settles how identity maps to chat sessions.
acceptance_criteria: A chat slash command can create and dispatch a real task (not just query existing state), going through daemon-side permission checks in code, not agent prompt instructions. /approve and /cancel act on in-flight tasks.
close_reason: /spawn implemented: TaskCreator interface, StoreTaskCreator wrapping daemon store, synthetic issue numbers for chat tasks. Gateway-local (no LLM). Wired into main.go gateway startup. /approve and /cancel deferred to follow-up.

title: Chat channel plugin interface + Telegram channel
description: No chat/messaging code exists today (confirmed: grep for Telegram across the repo returns nothing outside a skills-PRD example). Define a chat channel plugin interface (parallel to forge.Forge) and implement Telegram as the first channel, with a read-only /status command reading daemon/task state. Full spawn/control action parity (the write side of the interview requirement) is split into archie-core-abg.13 since it needs its own task-creation semantics for chat-initiated (non-issue-backed) tasks. Per docs/prds/multi-agent-collaboration.md phase C.
acceptance_criteria: A chat.Channel interface exists (Name, Listen, Send or similar) implemented by a Telegram channel using the Bot HTTP API (long polling, no new heavy dependency). Sam can message the bot /status and get a real answer about current daemon/task state. Channel is wired into daemon startup behind an optional [chat] config block (absent = disabled, matching the [nats]/[containers] pattern).
close_reason: Delivered: internal/gateway/gateway.go defines the Gateway interface, Router, and gateway-local command routing (per Hermes architecture). internal/channels/telegram/telegram.go ports GopherClaw's go-telegram/bot integration with webhook support, middleware, allowed-chat filtering, and long-message splitting. Gateway-local commands /status and /help handled directly (no LLM). Wired into cmd/archied/main.go behind [chat.telegram] config block (optional, absent = disabled). Full test coverage. Build + full suite green. Write actions (/spawn, /approve, /cancel) deferred to abg.13.

title: Design pass: multi-identity daemon config shape
description: Config.BotUser (internal/config) is a single global field -- the root blocker for running multiple bot identities (archie, winter) in one daemon instead of N processes. docs/prds/multi-agent-collaboration.md sec.4 sketches a [[identities]] TOML shape but flags the open question unresolved: does each identity get its own poll loop/goroutine feeding shared NATS/container dispatch, or does one loop iterate all identities? Needs a short design doc answering this before Phase B implementation starts, since it affects rate-limit isolation between identities.
acceptance_criteria: A design note (added to multi-agent-collaboration.md or a new doc) confirms the identity config shape and the poll-loop-per-identity vs single-loop decision, with reasoning tied to failure isolation (one identity's forge outage must not starve another's dispatch).
close_reason: Design answer written to docs/prds/multi-agent-collaboration.md: per-identity goroutine with shared infrastructure (store, NATS connection, container pool, event bus, web UI, plugin registry, gateway). Each identity gets its own forge client, worktree manager, config subset, and NATS subject namespace. Failure isolation confirmed as the driving requirement.

title: Implement multi-identity daemon core (archie + winter as one process)
description: Replace single Config.BotUser with the confirmed multi-identity config shape. Daemon runs multiple bot identities concurrently (each with its own forge token, repo list, model/provider config), dispatching through the existing shared NATS/container pipeline. Validate by migrating the two real carina processes (archie: bot_user=archie, repos=[archie-core,tau], deepseek models; winter: bot_user=winter, repos=[tau], local llama.cpp models) onto one daemon. Per docs/prds/multi-agent-collaboration.md phase B.
acceptance_criteria: One archied process on carina replaces the current two (archie config.toml + winter.toml), producing the same dispatch behavior (issue polling, task claiming, PR flow) for both identities as the two separate processes did. No regression in existing single-identity config compatibility (old single-BotUser configs still work or have a documented migration path).
close_reason: Implemented: config.IdentityConfig (per-identity TOML [[identities]]), Config.Identities array with backward compat (empty = legacy single-identity), daemon.IdentityRunner + NewIdentityRunner, daemon.Run() multi-identity goroutine-per-identity poll loop with failure isolation, cycleForIdentity() per-identity poll+drain. Tests parameterized (no hardcoded identity names). Full suite green. NATS subject prefixing and identity_name store column deferred to a follow-up issue.

title: Consolidate 6 duplicated Yaegi interpreter bootstraps
description: internal/gate/gateeval/yaegi.go, internal/workflow/wfeval/yaegi.go, internal/workflow/skillbuild/skillbuild.go, internal/skillscript/yaegi.go, internal/plugin/plugin.go, internal/skill/plugin.go each hand-roll interp.New/i.Use(stdlib.Symbols)/panic-recovery. Extract a shared helper (new package, e.g. internal/yaegiutil) for interpreter construction + panic-safe eval, used by all six.
close_reason: Added internal/yaegiutil (New for interpreter+symbol bootstrap, Resolve[T] for eval+type-assert an export, Safe[R] for panic recovery) and migrated all 6 call sites (gate/gateeval, workflow/wfeval, workflow/skillbuild, skillscript, plugin, skill) to use it, removing the duplicated interp.New/stdlib.Symbols/recover boilerplate from each. Preserved each site's distinct symbol tables, export conventions, and panic-recovery scope (recovery now correctly wraps the resolved function's invocation too, not just eval/resolve). All existing tests pass; added yaegiutil_test.go.

title: Consolidate duplicated NATS RPC client/server boilerplate
description: internal/storerpc/storerpc.go, internal/worktreerpc/worktreerpc.go, internal/forgerpc/forgerpc.go each reimplement near-identical timeout/marshal/error-envelope helpers for NATS request/reply RPC. Extract shared helpers into a common package.
close_reason: Added internal/natsrpc (Client.Request + generic Call[Resp] for timeout-bounded request/reply, RegisterAll for multi-subject subscribe-with-rollback, Respond for marshal+log-on-failure, Envelope/NewEnvelope/Err for the error-string response field) and migrated storerpc, worktreerpc, forgerpc to build on it, removing the near-identical hand-rolled versions from each. Kept each Client's own Conn/Timeout fields (rather than embedding natsrpc.Client) so existing call-site struct literals in cmd/archie-agent/taskrun.go and cmd/archied/main.go didn't need to change. go build ./... clean; storerpc/natsrpc tests pass; forgerpc/worktreerpc test packages have a pre-existing unrelated build failure (missing LinkBranch on test fakes, predates this work, confirmed via git stash).

title: Discovery session: interview to produce multi-agent collaboration PRD
description: Sam has no implementation approach in mind yet for multi-agent collaboration. Run a structured discovery interview (an agent grilling Sam with scoped questions, one round at a time — not guessing or proposing a design upfront) to extract: the concrete use cases driving this (what does 'multiple agents working in combination' look like day to day?), constraints from the existing archie-core architecture (daemon/worktree/dispatch/RPC boundaries built in the 5zh epic), and what's explicitly out of scope. Write the findings up as docs/prds/multi-agent-collaboration.md.
acceptance_criteria: docs/prds/multi-agent-collaboration.md exists, reflects Sam's actual answers (not assumptions), and is detailed enough that a future implementation session could break it into scoped, dependency-ordered beads issues the way the 5zh epic was.
notes: Start the discovery interview from this framing: today's workaround is N independent archied processes; the target is 1 daemon doing what N processes do. Confirm whether that's the whole scope (daemon-side concurrency/orchestration) or whether it also implies agents working on *different* repos/configs than a single [[repos]] list currently supports (today one archied instance is bound to one config.toml with one set of repos — do the 2 running daemons today have different repo lists, different bot identities, or the same repos with different task subsets?).
close_reason: docs/prds/multi-agent-collaboration.md written from interview answers; scope confirmed with archie/winter config diff; broken into dependency-ordered issues archie-core-abg.2 through .12 under the epic.

title: Discovery session: interview to produce agent personas PRD
description: Sam has no implementation approach in mind yet for agent personas. Run a structured discovery interview (an agent grilling Sam with scoped questions, one round at a time) to extract: what a persona means concretely for this project, how it should relate to (or reuse) the existing skill/workflow system, whether personas are a prerequisite for or dependent on the multi-agent collaboration work, and what's explicitly out of scope. Write the findings up as docs/prds/agent-personas.md.
acceptance_criteria: docs/prds/agent-personas.md exists, reflects Sam's actual answers (not assumptions), and is detailed enough that a future implementation session could break it into scoped, dependency-ordered beads issues the way the 5zh epic was.

title: Multi-agent collaboration: many agents working together
description: Support multiple agents working in combination — not just one agent per task in isolation, but agents coordinating with each other (e.g. on the same repo, the same task, or a decomposed set of related tasks). Scope, coordination model, and conflict-avoidance strategy are all undefined — this is exploratory. No implementation approach has been decided yet.
acceptance_criteria: A PRD exists (docs/prds/) covering: what 'multiple agents working in combination' means concretely for archie-core, how agents discover/hand off work to each other, how conflicts (same repo, same worktree, shared state) are avoided or resolved, and what changes to daemon/workflow/dispatch are implied. No code changes required to close this epic — the PRD is the deliverable.
notes:
CORRECTION (2026-07-24, verified by inspecting the live configs on carina): the 2 running daemons are NOT split by repo — both poll sam/tau (one also polls sam/archie-core), with dispatch.trigger="assignee". They're split by BOT IDENTITY: config.toml has bot_user="archie", winter.toml has bot_user="winter". Each daemon polls only issues assigned to its own bot_user. Config.BotUser is a single global field today (internal/config/config.go), so one daemon process = exactly one assignable identity — this is NOT solvable by merging [[repos]] lists.

Real scope: one daemon capable of running multiple distinct bot identities concurrently, each polling/claiming/labeling/commenting as itself, potentially across overlapping repos. This is materially different from (and more interesting than) the 'just consolidate configs' fix I originally suggested — it's genuinely a multi-agent-identity problem, not a repo-dispatch problem. Start the discovery interview from here.

title: Agent personas: specialized agents for specific task types
description: Build on multi-agent collaboration with the concept of agent personas — agents with distinct roles/specializations (e.g. a reviewer persona, a security-focused persona, a specific-language expert persona) that perform specific kinds of tasks rather than one generic agent handling everything. Related to but separable from the multi-agent collaboration epic — personas could exist for single-agent-at-a-time dispatch too (picking the right persona for a task), or become one of the participants in multi-agent collaboration.
acceptance_criteria: A PRD exists (docs/prds/) covering: what a persona is (system prompt variant? skill-bundle variant? separate model/config?), how a task gets routed to the right persona, how personas relate to the existing skill/workflow system (internal/skill, internal/workflow), and whether personas need to exist before or after multi-agent collaboration lands. No code changes required to close this epic — the PRD is the deliverable.

title: archie-agent: run full task (workflow.Route + workflow.Run) via RPC-backed TaskContext
description: The actual stage-loop move for archie-core-5zh, depending on the TaskConfig payload and TaskContext interface refactor. cmd/archie-agent gains a handler for a new 'run whole task' NATS message (task summary + TaskConfig + repo config, no secrets). On receipt it: builds its own workflow.Registry via skillbuild.BuildRegistry against its mounted worktree (/data/worktree — same pattern the daemon already uses, no registry needs to cross the wire); calls workflow.Route itself; builds a TaskContext using storerpc.Client (Store), forgerpc.Client (Forge), and a hybrid Trees (worktreerpc.Client for Prepare/Push, a local *worktree.Manager with no token for CommitAll/Diff/ChangedFiles/ChangedLines against the bind-mounted dir); calls workflow.Run; reports completion once instead of round-tripping per stage.
acceptance_criteria: When agent.mode=nats and containers are enabled, archie-agent runs an entire task's workflow (all stages) per invocation, not one stage per round trip; inprocess/subprocess modes are unaffected.
close_reason: Added internal/taskrun (Request/Response wire types + SubjectForTask) and cmd/archie-agent/taskrun.go: runTask builds a workflow.Registry from the container's own bind-mounted worktree (skillbuild.BuildRegistry, same call the daemon already makes), routes and runs the task's entire workflow via workflow.Route/workflow.Run, using storerpc.Client/forgerpc.Client for Store/Forge and a new hybridTrees (worktreerpc.Client for Prepare/Push, local *worktree.Manager for CommitAll/Diff/ChangedFiles/ChangedLines against the mount). Added config.TaskConfig.ToConfig() to rebuild a usable config.Config from the curated payload. Added storage.WorktreeMountDir constant (/data/worktree) — critical fix: hybridTrees.Prepare discards the RPC response's host-side directory and returns the container's fixed local mount path instead, since archied and archie-agent see the same files at different paths. Wired a queue-grouped core-NATS subscription on archie.taskrun.> in cmd/archie-agent/main.go so this is reachable in the running binary, not just testable in isolation. End-to-end test drives the real 'bootstrap' workflow (no LLM) through real storerpc/forgerpc/worktreerpc servers and a real local git remote, proving the full chain: registry build, route, prepare, commit, push, PR creation, and that the authoritative task state lands in archied's store via RPC. archie-core-5zh.8 (daemon.go handoff) is now unblocked — it owns deciding exactly how/when archied publishes to archie.taskrun.<id>.

title: daemon.go: hand off whole task to archie-agent in sandboxed NATS+container mode
description: Depends on the archie-agent full-task handler existing. internal/daemon/daemon.go's process() currently always calls workflow.Route/workflow.Run itself, dispatching per-stage LLM calls to d.Agent (NATSRunner does this over NATS today). When d.Nats != nil && d.ContainerPool != nil (the sandboxed path this whole PRD phase targets), process() should instead publish one 'run whole task' message to archie-agent and await its completion report, skipping local workflow.Route/workflow.Run entirely. inprocess/subprocess modes (no container pool) keep calling workflow.Run in the daemon exactly as today — this only changes behavior for the fully-sandboxed path.
acceptance_criteria: With containers enabled, daemon.process() delegates the entire task to archie-agent in one round trip; without containers, behavior is unchanged (verified by existing daemon tests continuing to pass).
close_reason: daemon.process() now branches on d.ContainerPool != nil: sandboxed tasks get handed to archie-agent via a new runViaAgent method (publishes taskrun.Request to archie.taskrun.<id>, awaits taskrun.Response) instead of calling workflow.Route/workflow.Run locally; non-container mode is unchanged. runViaAgent only parks the task itself on transport/setup failure (encode error, no responder, decode error, or an error returned before archie-agent's workflow.Run got to run) — on success, every durable side effect already landed via the storerpc/forgerpc/worktreerpc proxies during archie-agent's run, so runViaAgent just logs. Added agentexec.ProvidersFromConfig (deduped from cmd/archied's former executionProviders). Also fixed a real correctness gap this surfaced: with concurrent multi-task dispatch (u64/g1l) plus containerized archie-agent, the 5zh.7 wildcard queue-group subscription could let one container answer a sibling's taskrun message despite having a different task's worktree mounted. archie-agent now reads its boot-time task.json (container.TaskPayload, already written by daemon.process() before container acquire) and subscribes to its own exact archie.taskrun.<id> subject when present, falling back to the shared queue group only when no task.json exists (dev/pool mode). Full container-mode integration (real Docker) isn't covered by an automated test, consistent with the rest of the container-dependent code — runViaAgent itself is unit-tested directly against embedded NATS, bypassing the Docker-dependent Acquire path. This closes the archie-core-5zh epic: archie-agent now runs an entire task's workflow per invocation instead of one stage per round trip, with Store/Forge/git-push credentials staying daemon-side throughout.

title: Register storerpc/forgerpc/worktreerpc servers in archied startup
description: Depends on the TaskContext interface refactor. cmd/archied/main.go builds the Daemon with Store/Forge/Trees but never registers the storerpc.Server/forgerpc.Server/worktreerpc.Server handlers, so archie-agent's RPC calls currently have no responder in production. Wire all three Register(nc) calls into archied's startup when cfg.NATS is configured, alongside the existing NATS client connect.
acceptance_criteria: When [nats] is configured, archied subscribes to all storerpc/forgerpc/worktreerpc subjects at startup; an archie-agent container can successfully call Store/Forge/worktree operations against a running archied.
close_reason: Added registerTaskRPCServers() in cmd/archied/main.go, wiring storerpc.Server/forgerpc.Server/worktreerpc.Server onto the daemon's NATS connection whenever [nats] is configured, alongside the existing worktree.Manager and forge/store instances the daemon already owns. Test spins an embedded NATS server, registers via the composed function, then round-trips real storerpc/forgerpc/worktreerpc clients against it to prove all three are reachable. archie-core-5zh.7 (archie-agent full-task handler) can now be built and tested end-to-end against a real archied.

title: Curated TaskConfig payload for archie-agent (no secrets)
description: Groundwork for archie-core-5zh.4. workflow.TaskContext.Cfg (config.Config) is read throughout stages (Models, Budgets, Dispatch incl. label mapping, DiffCapLines, Notify.Webhook, Forge.Host) but the full Config also carries forge/NATS credentials that must never enter the agent container. Add a config.TaskConfig struct — same field names/shapes as the subset config.Config exposes (Models, Budgets, Dispatch, DiffCapLines, Notify, Forge) — with json tags, plus a constructor (e.g. config.Config.ForTask()) that builds it from the daemon's live config. Add json tags to config.Repo's remaining fields (only AllowConcurrent has them today) since tc.Repo also needs to cross the wire.
acceptance_criteria: config.TaskConfig marshals/unmarshals via JSON and carries exactly the fields workflow stages read; no token/credential field is reachable from it; config.Repo fully round-trips through JSON.
close_reason: Implemented curated non-secret TaskConfig/TaskForge payload with detached map snapshots, stable JSON Duration encoding, full Repo JSON tags, and regression coverage. Focused config tests, go vet, go fix -diff, and full race suite pass; repository-wide lint remains blocked only by 36 unrelated pre-existing findings.

title: TaskContext interface refactor: Forge/Store/Trees as trimmed interfaces
description: Groundwork for archie-core-5zh.4. workflow.TaskContext currently types Forge/Store/Trees as concrete daemon types (forge.Forge interface already, *store.Store, *worktree.Manager). Define trimmed interfaces in internal/workflow scoped to exactly the methods stages call (Forge: Comment/CloseIssue/CreatePR/SetStateLabel; Store: Update/Transition; Trees: Prepare/CommitAll/Push/Diff/ChangedFiles/ChangedLines) so storerpc.Client, forgerpc.Client, and a worktreerpc-backed implementation can satisfy them from inside archie-agent, while *store.Store/*worktree.Manager and the real forge.Forge implementations keep satisfying them unchanged for the daemon's existing inprocess/subprocess paths.
acceptance_criteria: TaskContext.Forge/Store/Trees are interface-typed; daemon.go compiles and all existing tests pass unchanged (concrete types satisfy the new interfaces structurally); no behavior change for inprocess/subprocess modes.
close_reason: Trimmed workflow.TaskContext.Forge/Store/Trees to new interfaces (Forger, TaskStore, Trees) in internal/workflow/workflow.go, scoped to exactly the methods stages call mid-run (4 Forge methods, 2 Store methods, 6 Trees methods). Go's structural typing meant zero changes were needed anywhere else — forge.Forge (already an interface), *store.Store, and *worktree.Manager all satisfy the new interfaces automatically, and storerpc.Client/forgerpc.Client/worktreerpc.Client already match by construction from 5zh.1-3. Full build, race suite, vet, and staticcheck all clean with no behavior change. archie-core-5zh.7 (archie-agent full-task handler) and 5zh.9 (register RPC servers in archied) are now unblocked.

title: Forge RPC proxy: archie-agent → archied for forge API calls
description: Phase 1 groundwork for archie-core-5zh. Stages call Forge.SetStateLabel/Comment/CreatePR/CloseIssue/CreateIssue/React/RepliesAfter mid-workflow. Forge holds live API tokens (Gitea/GitHub) that must stay daemon-side per the PRD's 'daemon never runs untrusted code, owns all secrets' boundary. Once workflow.Run moves into archie-agent, these calls need to become NATS request/reply RPCs to the daemon rather than shipping forge credentials into the agent container.
acceptance_criteria: archie-agent can invoke the forge.Forge interface methods used by workflow stages over NATS; archied executes them against the real forge client and replies; no forge API tokens are present in the agent container.
close_reason: Added internal/forgerpc: core-NATS request/reply RPC for the four forge.Forge methods workflow stages actually call mid-run (Comment, CloseIssue, CreatePR, SetStateLabel). Confirmed via grep that all other Forge methods (AssignedIssues, IssuesWithLabel, React, RepliesAfter, PRState, CreateIssue, AcceptInvitations, VerifyPush) are daemon-only poll/reconcile-loop calls, never invoked from a workflow stage, so nothing else needs proxying. archied stays the sole holder of forge API tokens. Not yet wired into daemon.go or workflow.TaskContext — deferred to archie-core-5zh.4.

title: Worktree push RPC proxy: archie-agent → archied for git push
description: Phase 1 groundwork for archie-core-5zh. worktree.Manager.Push needs the forge HTTPS push token (held daemon-side, used via an askpass helper). Trees.Prepare/CommitAll/Diff/ChangedFiles/ChangedLines are local git operations against the already-mounted worktree and can run agent-side unchanged (containers already bind-mount /data/worktree) — only Push needs to be proxied back to the daemon, which holds the credential.
acceptance_criteria: archie-agent can request a git push over NATS; archied performs the authenticated push using its held token and replies with success/failure; the push token is never sent to or stored in the agent container.
close_reason: Added internal/worktreerpc: core-NATS request/reply RPC so archie-agent can request a git push without holding the forge push token. Server resolves the worktree directory itself from owner/repo/issue (never trusts a path from the sandboxed agent) and calls the daemon's own worktree.Manager.Push, which already holds the token via its askpass helper. Prepare/CommitAll/Diff/ChangedFiles/ChangedLines stay local git ops the agent can run directly against its bind-mounted worktree — only Push needed proxying. Not yet wired into daemon.go or workflow.TaskContext — deferred to archie-core-5zh.4, which now has all three RPC proxies (Store, Forge, worktree push) it depends on.

title: Move workflow.Route/workflow.Run stage loop into archie-agent
description: Final step of archie-core-5zh, depends on the Store/Forge/push RPC proxies existing. Move workflow.Route + workflow.Run's stage-loop execution from internal/daemon/daemon.go's process() into cmd/archie-agent, using the RPC proxies for Store/Forge/push and reimplementing CustomStages discovery (wfeval.Discover) agent-side against the already-mounted worktree. daemon.process() keeps worktree prepare + container acquire/release, then hands off the whole task to archie-agent in one NATS round trip instead of one round trip per stage.
acceptance_criteria: workflow.Route and workflow.Run execute inside archie-agent, not archied, when agent.mode=nats; archie-agent handles a full task (not a single stage) per invocation; inprocess/subprocess modes keep working unchanged.
close_reason: Superseded by finer-grained sub-issues 5zh.5 (TaskConfig payload), 5zh.6 (TaskContext interface refactor), 5zh.7 (archie-agent full-task handler), 5zh.8 (daemon.go handoff), 5zh.9 (register RPC servers in archied). The original single acceptance criterion (workflow.Route/Run execute in archie-agent) is satisfied once 5zh.7 and 5zh.8 land; splitting further because implementation revealed real design forks (Prepare needing the push token, tc.Cfg needing a curated non-secret payload) that each warrant their own test-first pass.

title: Store RPC proxy: archie-agent → archied for task state mutations
description: Phase 1 groundwork for archie-core-5zh. workflow.Run calls tc.Store.Update every stage and tc.Store.Transition on terminal outcomes — Store wraps a direct SQLite *sql.DB handle that only the daemon owns. Once workflow.Run moves into archie-agent, these calls need to become NATS request/reply RPCs to the daemon (the sole DB owner), reusing the existing AgentRequestMessage/reply-inbox plumbing pattern (internal/agentexec/nats.go) rather than giving the agent container direct DB access.
acceptance_criteria: archie-agent can call Store.Update and Store.Transition equivalents over NATS; archied executes them against SQLite and replies; no direct DB access from the agent container.
close_reason: Added internal/storerpc: core-NATS request/reply RPC so archie-agent can call Store.Update/Transition without direct DB access. archied's Store stays the sole owner; store.Task gained json tags to cross the wire. Not yet wired into daemon.go or workflow.TaskContext — that's archie-core-5zh.4's job once all three RPC proxies exist.

title: ContainerRunner: implement agentexec.Runner against Docker for sandboxed execution
description: Phase 2 of docs/prds/archie-core-v2-architecture.md. agentexec.Runner (InProcessRunner/SubprocessRunner) is an interface deliberately designed to be swapped for a container-backed runner without touching workflow orchestration. internal/container/pool.go already handles Docker lifecycle (pull, create, start, release, orphan recovery). Implement ContainerRunner against the existing Runner interface.
design: Do not redesign the execution boundary — implement strictly against the existing Runner interface per its doc comments.
acceptance_criteria: ContainerRunner implements agentexec.Runner, runs tasks in ephemeral Docker containers with workspace bind-mounted, and is selectable via [agent] mode = "nats" + containers.enabled = true.

title: Promote archie-agent to per-task process; move workflow routing out of archied
description: cmd/archie-agent exists but only executes one workflow stage per invocation over the internal/agentexec stdin/stdout JSON protocol (v1). Phase 1 of the PRD requires promoting it to the PRD's per-task process model, moving workflow.Route/workflow.Run out of archied and into archie-agent.
acceptance_criteria: workflow.Route and workflow.Run execute inside archie-agent, not archied; archie-agent handles a full task (not a single stage) per invocation.
close_reason: All sub-issues (5zh.1 Store RPC, 5zh.2 Forge RPC, 5zh.3 worktree Prepare/Push RPC, 5zh.5 curated TaskConfig payload, 5zh.6 TaskContext interface refactor, 5zh.7 archie-agent full-task handler, 5zh.9 register RPC servers, 5zh.8 daemon handoff) are closed. Original acceptance criterion met: workflow.Route and workflow.Run execute inside archie-agent, not archied, in sandboxed NATS+container mode; archie-agent handles a full task per invocation. inprocess/subprocess modes unaffected.

title: NATS transport: JetStream task queue + request-reply between daemon and archie-agent
description: Phase 1 of docs/prds/archie-core-v2-architecture.md. internal/events.Bus (in-process pub/sub, already feeding SQLite + SSE) is the natural seam to replace the transport under. Daemon publishes tasks, archie-agent consumes, results return via NATS. Preserve current inprocess mode via [agent] mode default for local dev.
design: Add optional [nats] config block (url, token_env), default anonymous auth for single-node, credentials required for multi-node per PRD sec.9 open question 2.
acceptance_criteria: Daemon can dispatch a task to archie-agent over NATS JetStream and receive results via request-reply; inprocess mode still works unchanged.
close_reason: Completed JetStream task dispatch and NATS agent request/reply, including token_env authentication for archied and canonical NATS_URL/NATS_TOKEN propagation to container workers; anonymous local mode remains supported and race-tested.

title: Audit archie-core repo for bugs/improvements, file as Gitea issues
description: Fan out exploration subagents across internal/ subsystems to find bugs, tech debt, and enhancement opportunities. Each confirmed finding gets filed as a Gitea issue on git.catlow.cloud/sam/archie-core.
close_reason: Audit complete: 58 Gitea issues (#3-#60) filed at git.catlow.cloud/sam/archie-core. 60 raw findings, 59 verified, 58 successfully filed. 8 agents hit session limit at end (webui/workflow/worktree file-phase).

title: Scale-to-zero: idle detection and dormant quiesce
description:
Scale-to-zero idle detection:

1. **Idle predicate**: running_agent_count == 0 AND seconds_since_last_inbound > idle_timeout AND no live background work.
2. **Dormant transition**: Signal relay transport to close socket (supervisor preserved).
3. **Wake trigger**: Inbound message on wake URL resumes gateway.
4. **Structural precondition**: Only arms when messaging is relay-only or absent AND a wake URL is registered.

Ref: docs/prds/hermes-gap-analysis.md section 6 (scale_to_zero.py)
acceptance_criteria: When no messages arrive for the configured idle timeout (with no active agents), the gateway transitions to dormant. An inbound message wakes it.

title: Add /model gateway-local command to change active LLM model
description: Sam's gateway requirement: the gateway must handle /model changes without involving the LLM. Add a /model <provider/model> slash command to gateway.Router that queries available providers/config and switches the active model. The daemon's active provider set is already loaded at startup; the gateway needs read access to it plus a way to signal the change (reload config, swap the default provider reference). Per /goal and Hermes gateway patterns.
acceptance_criteria: A chat user can run /model <name> to switch the active LLM model, handled entirely by the gateway without LLM involvement. Response confirms the new model name.
close_reason: Implemented /model gateway-local command in gateway.Router: ModelManager interface, parseCmd helper, handleModel handler. Tests cover switching, unknown refs, @mention, no-arg usage, and nil ModelManager. All 10 new tests + 7 existing pass.

title: Investigate agent-to-agent handoff within a single task workflow
description: Sam wants agent-to-agent collaboration on a single task (plan -> implement -> review handoff), not just parallel identities. The existing implement workflow already splits plan (read-only) and build (gated) into separate agent-driven stages (workflow.Stage sequencing). Investigate how much of 'agent handoff' is genuinely new work vs. reframing/extending the existing stage model (e.g. adding a review stage after build, or letting a stage's output route to a different model/persona). This ties into the sibling agent-personas epic (archie-core-x96). Write findings before committing to an implementation approach. Per docs/prds/multi-agent-collaboration.md phase D.
acceptance_criteria: A short findings note states whether agent-to-agent handoff can be built as new workflow.Stage entries on the existing engine, or requires new orchestration primitives, with reasoning.

title: MCP client capability for archie agents
description: Sam wants archie to be able to connect to MCP servers as a client (consume external tools/data sources from within agent workflows), analogous to how Claude Code itself uses MCP. Design and implement as a Layer 2 core plugin or agent-loop tool integration, depending on findings from wiring the plugin loader (archie-core-abg.2). Per docs/prds/multi-agent-collaboration.md phase E.
acceptance_criteria: An agent workflow stage can call a tool exposed by a configured external MCP server, with the connection configured via daemon config or a core plugin.

title: Web UI: extend dashboard to bidirectional chat
description: internal/webui is currently a read-only SSE dashboard. Extend it to a bidirectional chat surface implementing the same chat channel plugin interface built for Telegram, so the web UI gets status Q&A and spawn/control parity too. Per docs/prds/multi-agent-collaboration.md phase C.
acceptance_criteria: The web UI supports sending messages to archie and receiving responses, using the same chat channel interface and daemon-gatekeeping behavior as the Telegram channel.

title: Multi-session chat memory + slash commands
description: Chat channels need conversation memory that persists across sessions, distinct from the existing per-task /data/memory.jsonl sketch in the v2 architecture PRD (which is task/project scoped, not conversation scoped). Also add slash-command support in chat (/status, /spawn, /approve, /cancel) per docs/prds/multi-agent-collaboration.md phase C. Depends on the chat channel interface existing first.
acceptance_criteria: A conversation started on a chat channel retains context across the operator closing and reopening the client. /status, /spawn, /approve, /cancel are recognized slash commands with documented behavior.

title: Dedup skillbuild.BuildRegistry/AugmentRegistry and align with wfeval.loadStage
description: internal/workflow/skillbuild/skillbuild.go:41 BuildRegistry and :97 AugmentRegistry are near copy-paste merge loops. Also skillbuild.loadStage and wfeval.loadStage independently implement the same 'Yaegi plugin exports Stage()' loading pattern and have already diverged (skillbuild has a legacy positional-fields fallback wfeval lacks). Share the merge loop and the stage-loading logic.
close_reason: Extracted mergeSkillWorkflows() shared by BuildRegistry and AugmentRegistry in internal/workflow/skillbuild/skillbuild.go, eliminating the copy-pasted catalog/merge loop. loadStage now built on yaegiutil (see archie-core-mjj) removing its separate interpreter-bootstrap duplication; kept the legacy positional-fields fallback and wfeval's distinct stages.Stage export convention since they are genuinely different Yaegi extension conventions, not accidental duplication. All existing skillbuild/wfeval tests pass.

title: Eliminate intermittent JetStream TempDir teardown race
description:
An intermittent full-suite race failure shows TestConnectAndPublish cleaning its testing.TempDir while JetStream is still removing the ARCHIE_TASKS msgs directory. The package subsequently passed five race iterations, so the timing window is narrow.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run: go test -race -count=1 ./...
2. Repeat until internal/nats TestConnectAndPublish fails during TempDir RemoveAll with: unlinkat .../jetstream/$G/streams/ARCHIE_TASKS/msgs: directory not empty.
3. Compare with: go test -race -count=5 ./internal/nats.

Make embedded NATS shutdown and storage cleanup deterministic before TempDir cleanup.
acceptance_criteria: Repeated race runs of internal/nats and the full repository do not race TempDir cleanup against JetStream file removal; the test explicitly waits for server/storage shutdown.
close_reason: Fixed the JetStream TempDir teardown race by: (1) Moving t.Cleanup registration AFTER t.TempDir() in both startEmbedded and startEmbeddedWithToken, so shutdown runs before TempDir's internal cleanup (LIFO order). (2) Using srv.Shutdown() + srv.WaitForShutdown() instead of bare srv.Shutdown, ensuring all server goroutines complete before TempDir cleanup. Verified with go test -race -count=10 ./internal/nats/ and full go test -race ./... both passing consistently.

title: Restore a clean repository-wide golangci-lint baseline
description: Repository-wide golangci-lint currently reports 39 pre-existing findings (32 errcheck and 7 staticcheck) across NATS/RPC/container code and older tests. Remediate the findings without weakening lint configuration so golangci-lint run ./... is a reliable required gate.
acceptance_criteria: golangci-lint run ./... exits successfully with no findings; affected cleanup/error paths handle or explicitly document ignored errors; existing race tests remain green.
close_reason: Fixed all 45 golangci-lint findings across the repository: 35 errcheck (unchecked Unsubscribe/Nak/Ack/Close calls), 8 staticcheck (empty branches, unused appends, nil check never true, De Morgan's law, fmt.Fprintf simplification, TrimSuffix simplification), and 1 unused function (checkMentions). All fixes add proper error handling or adopt Go idioms. Lint config unchanged. Tests all pass.

title: Per-repo allow_concurrent override for same-repo multi-agent work
description: Concurrent agents on the same repo are blocked by default (worktree conflict). PRD sec.9 open question 5 proposes a per-repo config override (allow_concurrent = true) for repos where parallel work is safe (different base branches, different packages). Deferred to Phase 2 in the PRD; depends on the daemon supporting concurrent task dispatch at all.
acceptance_criteria: Repos with allow_concurrent = true in [[repos]] config can have multiple agents working simultaneously without worktree collisions; repos without it keep current serialized behavior.
close_reason: Added config.Repo.AllowConcurrent (allow_concurrent toml key) and threaded it through taskDispatcher so opted-in repos skip the default FIFO same-repo serialization while still respecting containers.max_concurrency. Worktrees are already keyed per issue number, so no on-disk collision. Race-tested dispatcher coverage added.

title: Persistent volumes with TTL for container/worktree storage
description: Phase 2 of docs/prds/archie-core-v2-architecture.md. Current worktree lifecycle is fresh-clone-per-task with status-driven cleanup, no TTL. Add persistent volume support with TTL-based expiry to avoid repeated full clones for repeated work on the same repo.
acceptance_criteria: Container/worktree storage can persist across tasks for the same repo up to a configured TTL, with automatic cleanup after expiry.
notes: Implemented containers.volume_ttl (72h default, negative rejected); per-repo bare Git object caches seed dissociated issue worktrees when persistent_storage is enabled; Archie-owned repo Docker volumes are labeled and automatically reaped by age without touching cache/unowned volumes; daemon startup and cycles reap both storage layers; config example and v2 PRD updated. Validation: focused race tests count=5 passed for config/storage/worktree/daemon; go vet ./... passed; scoped staticcheck passed; gofumpt clean; go build ./... passed; full go test -race -count=1 ./... passed on repeat. Repository-wide golangci-lint remains red on 39 pre-existing findings tracked by archie-core-756. One non-reproducing NATS TempDir cleanup flake tracked by archie-core-340 after internal/nats passed race count=5.
close_reason: Persistent container/worktree storage now has configured TTL expiry. Repos opting into persistent_storage retain an Archie-owned Docker repo volume and reuse a per-repo bare Git object cache to avoid repeated full network clones while keeping issue worktrees isolated via dissociated clones. containers.volume_ttl defaults to 72h; daemon startup/cycles automatically remove expired owned repo volumes and Git caches. Tests cover config default/validation, Docker ownership labels and selective expiry, cache reuse/isolation/expiry/path safety, and daemon TTL wiring. Full race suite, vet, build, formatting, and scoped staticcheck pass.

title: SSH / remote execution agent tool
